title: Smallest affine neighborhoods and smooth monoscheme product charts
statement:
Let $M$ be a fine monoscheme and $x\in M$ [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. There is a smallest open neighborhood $M_x$ of $x$, consisting of its generalizations, which is affine with section monoid $\mathcal M_x$. More explicitly, in an affine neighborhood $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$ with finite generating set $E$ and prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $x$, one has $M_x=D(a)$ and $\Gamma(M_x,\mathcal M)=P_{\mathfrak p}$, where $a$ is the sum of the members of $E\setminus\mathfrak p$ (the empty sum is $0$) and $P_{\mathfrak p}=P-(P\setminus\mathfrak p)$.

For a morphism $f:N\to M$ of fine monoschemes and $y\in N$, $f$ restricts to $N_y\to M_{f(y)}$, whose map of section monoids is the stalk map. If $f$ is smooth, this restriction is an affine chart induced by $P\to P\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ for finite $r,t\geq0$. For every field $k$, its realized ring map is the inclusion $k[P]\to k[P][x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_t^{\pm1}]$; the associated scheme morphism is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The source realizations of these neighborhoods cover $k[N]$. No torsion-freeness assumption is imposed on $M,N$.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.4(iii), 3.1.10(ii), 3.1.13--3.1.16 and Lemma 3.2.12(i), pp.98--100,104; polynomial/Laurent infinitesimal lifting argument expanded by an agent.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighborhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$ of $x$ and a finite generating set $E$. Apply [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood] to the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $x$. It gives $D(a)=\bigcap_{b\notin\mathfrak p}D(b)$, $a=\sum_{e\in E\setminus\mathfrak p}e$, and $P_a=P-(P\setminus\mathfrak p)$. A prime $\mathfrak q$ belongs to this intersection exactly when $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so these are exactly the generalizations of $x$. Every open neighborhood $V$ of $x$ in $M$ intersects $U$ in a neighborhood containing $D(a)$; consequently $D(a)$ is smallest also in $M$. By [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], its sections are $P_a$. Taking germs on a smallest neighborhood identifies its sections with the stalk, since every representative restricts there and equality of germs is equality after this restriction. Thus $M_x=D(a)$ and $\Gamma(M_x,\mathcal M)=P_{\mathfrak p}$. That this smallest neighborhood is affine, namely canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}\mathcal M_{M,x}$ with its ordinary monoid sheaf, is the first monoscheme clause of [lem-trf-fine-monoid-local-smooth-charts]. For the finite-generator section formula in the affine model, use the minimal-neighborhood theorem to obtain membership, minimality and the equality of localization submonoids. Every covering sieve on the smallest neighborhood contains its identity: choose a member containing the distinguished point and use minimality to show that member equals the whole open. The sheafification unit is locally injective and locally surjective, hence bijective there. Evaluation of a compatible fraction family at the distinguished point identifies the original presheaf sections with localization at its complementary face; the inverse is the constant family, which is locally a fraction everywhere because all prime complements contain this face. Compose this equivalence with the inverse sheafification unit. Naturality of that unit on the restriction from the whole spectrum proves the required formula on every numerator.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.4(iii) and Remark 3.1.10(ii), pp.98--100; finite-generator form from VIII 3.1.2--3.1.4.

proof.text: For x=f(y), continuity makes the inverse image of the smallest target neighborhood an open neighborhood of y. Source minimality gives the inclusion. Apply the universal property of the target open immersion to the source open inclusion followed by f; its factorization equality is an equality of full sheafed-space morphisms. The colimit equations for the canonical germ, colim.map, and colimit.pre show that taking a germ of a section pulled back and then restricted is the stalk map applied to its original germ. These constructions use only [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] and its actual sheaf morphisms.

source.place: VIII 3.1.6 and Remark 3.1.10(ii), pp.99--100; argument from smallest neighborhoods.

proof.text: A smallest neighborhood is terminal in the opposite category of open neighborhoods, since it is included in every neighborhood. Thus its canonical injection into the stalk colimit is an isomorphism, by Mathlib isIso_ι_of_isTerminal. This works for the actual filtered-colimit stalk of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], without assuming all colimits exist in CommMonCat. The definition of smoothness in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] supplies ranks r,t and a product splitting of the stalk map. Compose the target germ equivalence times the identity on the free factors, then this stalk splitting, then the inverse source germ equivalence. Applying the injective source germ and the naturality equation of the preceding step proves the required formula for every section. No separate smooth affine-chart theorem or torsion-freeness assumption is used.

Put P=Gamma(V), B=Multiplicative(Fin r -> N) and C=Multiplicative(Fin t -> Z). Transport along the given monoid equivalence backwards and permute the product factors to C x (B x P). Mathlib MonoidAlgebra.domCongr and curryAlgEquiv identify the algebra with k[P][B][C]. The finite-function/finitely-supported-function additive equivalence identifies the B algebra with MvPolynomial (Fin r) k[P], and toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv converts the C algebra to its additive notation. The single-basis formulas for these actual equivalences give precisely e^(p,alpha,beta) -> e^p x^alpha y^beta. Additive induction on monoid-algebra elements and the given equation e(p,1,1)=sectionMap(p) prove that the chart homomorphism becomes the coefficient inclusion. Only the concrete monoid-algebra construction of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] is needed; no torsion hypothesis enters.

source.place: VIII Lemma 3.2.12(i), p.104; the omitted product-algebra calculation expanded from VIII 3.2.1 and 3.1.16(i).

proof.text: For any commutative ring A, the algebra AddMonoidAlgebra A Z is LaurentPolynomial A, the localization of A[X] at X (Mathlib LaurentPolynomial.isLocalization). Algebra.Smooth.of_isLocalization_Away and Algebra.Smooth.comp show it is smooth over A. Induct on the finite Laurent rank: rank zero is A by AddMonoidAlgebra.uniqueAlgEquiv; split Fin(t+1) into its first coordinate and Fin t using Fin.consEquiv, and apply AddMonoidAlgebra.domCongr and curryAlgEquiv to identify the next algebra with a one-variable Laurent algebra over the preceding algebra. Transport smoothness along this algebra equivalence and compose. The polynomial algebra in Fin r is smooth, so the polynomial/Laurent coefficient inclusion is smooth. Step 4 identifies the realized ring map with this inclusion followed by the inverse ring equivalence; RingHom.Smooth.of_bijective and composition transport smoothness to that map. HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff for scheme Smooth concludes. Both zero ranks, arbitrary characteristic and torsion in P are retained. This uses Mathlib algebra smoothness directly rather than a scheme affine-space comparison.

source.place: Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; Tag 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth (empty relation list); Tags 01VA and 01VC, lemma-composition-smooth and lemma-open-immersion-smooth. Expands ILO VIII Lemma 3.2.12(i).

proof.text: For every commutative monoid Q, the nonunits form a proper prime monoid ideal m: 1 is a unit, a product is a unit exactly when both factors are units, and multiplication cannot turn a nonunit into a unit. A proper monoid ideal contains no unit, since multiplying a unit by its inverse would put 1, hence every element, in the ideal. Consequently every basic open containing m contains every prime. Induction over the generated topology proves that every prime specializes to m. In any affine open V of N, transport m through the chart homeomorphism to y. Every point of V specializes to y, so lies in the chosen smallest neighborhood U(y); minimality also gives U(y) contained in V. Thus U(y)=V as affine opens. By [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], the realization is the colimit of the locally directed affine diagram with open-immersion transition maps. Mathlib Scheme.IsLocallyDirected.ι_jointly_surjective gives an affine chart containing each realization point; replace that chart by the equal U(y). In the empty case the same joint-surjectivity statement proves the result without choosing any point of N.

source.place: VIII 3.1.4(i), 3.1.10(ii), 3.1.16(i) and 3.2.1, pp.98--101,103; covering argument expanded.

proof_origin.place: VIII Remarks 3.1.4(iii), 3.1.10(ii), 3.1.16(i) and Lemma 3.2.12(i); explicit monomial and Laurent-principal-open arguments supplied by Q05.; C5 proves the restriction/product-on-sections clause directly from the filtered stalk colimit and smoothness definition, and the covering clause from the nonunit prime and Mathlib open-gluing joint surjectivity. H5 proves the affine finite-generator section formula using locally bijective sheafification and evaluation on the smallest neighborhood, and the realized chart clause using explicit algebra currying and induction on Laurent variables. The first smallest-affine-neighborhood clause remains open.
